# upshot

Turn a chat conversation into a shareable link.

When the user says "export this", reply with a URL and nothing else. No
preamble, no code fence, no explanation.

Export what they pointed at, not the whole conversation. If they named a focus
("export this, mainly the part about x"), that is the scope. If not, use
whatever they were last discussing.

Write only what the conversation established. If it carries no verdict, put
what it does carry in `v` rather than inventing one. If the facts could have
changed recently and you can search, search first.

## Copy these

An answer with reasons:

https://upshot.fyi/v2/#a=Whether+to+move+the+API+off+Postgres&h=Stay+on+Postgres+for+now&v=SQLite+wins+on+ops%2C+but+you+need+concurrent+writes+within+the+year%2E&m=GPT-5&d=2026-09-10&g=Why&p=Concurrent+writes+are+the+one+thing+SQLite+cannot+do+at+your+scale%2E&p=The+ops+saving+is+real+but+small+-+about+two+hours+a+month%2E

A calculator, where the reader supplies the numbers:

https://upshot.fyi/v2/#a=Splitting+dinner+three+ways&h=About+twenty+seven+each&v=Service+is+already+in+the+total%2C+so+there+is+nothing+more+to+add%2E&m=GPT-5&d=2026-09-10&g=Split+it&i=Bill:80:bill&i=People:3:n&r=Each+pays:bill/n

A calculator in two stages, where a result feeds a later one:

https://upshot.fyi/v2/#a=The+most+I+can+offer+on+the+renovation&h=Work+backward+from+the+exit+value&v=Every+cost+comes+off+the+resale+price+before+the+offer+does%2E&m=GPT-5&d=2026-09-10&g=Exit&i=After+repair+value:450000:arv&i=Selling+cost+percent:7:sell&r=Selling+costs:arv%2A%28sell/100%29:exit&g=Offer&i=Renovation:70000:reno&i=Target+profit:60000:profit&r=Maximum+offer:arv-exit-reno-profit

An answer with boxes a formula can read:

## The frame

Always all five, always first.

- a  what the user asked, scoped to what they are exporting. Under 20 words.
- h  headline, under 12 words
- v  one sentence verdict, under 25 words
- m  your model name, e.g. GPT-5
- d  today's date, YYYY-MM-DD. If you are not certain what today is, ask.

## The blocks

Up to three. A `g=` starts a block and nothing else does, so one block holds
whatever mix of lines it needs.

- g  block label, 1 to 4 words
- p  bullet, under 35 words
- o  step, under 25 words. A how-to, where order is the point.
- c  checklist item, under 20 words. The reader can tick these off, and the
     ticks are kept in the link they hold. A formula can read them - see
     `ticks` below. Do not send `k=`.
- f  row, written `Label:Value`, e.g. `f=Cold+start:180ms`. One or two are
     drawn large, three or more become a spec sheet. You do not choose which.
- i  input, written `Label:Start:name`, e.g. `i=Seats:4:seats`. A box the
     reader types in, so the card is a tool rather than an answer. Their
     numbers are kept in the link they hold. Do not send `w=`.
- r  result, written `Label:Formula`, e.g. `r=Total:seats*price`. The card
     works it out and prints the formula beside it with every name replaced by
     what it held. Put the numbers into the formula rather than working them
     out yourself.
- t  decision, written `Label:Condition:When+true:When+false`, e.g.
     `t=Ready+to+walk:months>=target:Go+now:Not+yet`. The card tests the
     condition and prints the wording that applies, with the condition beside
     it. Four fields, always.

A comparison is two labelled blocks, and so is pros and cons:

    &g=Postgres&p=Concurrent+writes&p=Real+types
    &g=SQLite&p=Zero+ops&p=Faster+for+reads

## Formulas

A formula may use digits, `+ - * / ( )`, any name on the card,
`< > <= >= == !=`, and `min max round abs sqrt pow floor ceil`. Nothing else.

Two names are always there when the card has a checklist on it: `ticks` is how
many boxes are ticked, `boxes` how many there are. So a list the reader works
through can drive a score or a verdict - `r=Score:ticks/boxes*100` - and it
follows every tick. Do not name an input `ticks` or `boxes`.

A box can take a name too - `c=You+have+a+railcard:card` - and a formula reads
it as 1 when ticked and 0 when not. Name them when the options differ from
each other; use `ticks` when only how many matters.

`i` always ends with a short one-word name. `r` may take one, and a later
formula can use it: `r=Monthly:seats*price:mo` then `r=Per+year:mo*12`.

Name a step and reuse it rather than nesting brackets.

## Encoding

- Every space becomes `+`. The URL contains no spaces.
- Encode inside values: `,` %2C, `.` %2E, `(` %28, `)` %29, `*` %2A, `?` %3F,
  `&` %26, `#` %23, `+` %2B, `%` %25, `"` %22, and a `:` of your own as %3A.
- `=` `<` `>` in a condition are written as they are.
- A full stop inside a number is still a full stop: `4%2E5`, never `4.5`.
- No markdown and no line breaks inside a value.
- Under 2000 characters. If you are over: drop the weakest block, then the
  weakest lines in a block, then shorten the wording. Never drop the frame,
  never cut a value off mid-sentence.

## Before you reply

Check: no spaces, no bare `,` `.` `(` `)` `*` `?` inside any value, at most
three `g=`, every `i` name used by a formula, under 2000 characters.

Reply with the URL and nothing else.

## Version

v2, and the path says so: exports live at `https://upshot.fyi/v2/`. A later
version gets its own path, and `/v2/` keeps rendering every link ever written
against it, so an export you send today does not stop working when the format
moves on. `/v1/` is frozen and still renders links written before v2.

`/llms.txt` always describes the current version. A link written without the
path - `upshot.fyi/#a=...` - is forwarded to `/v2/`, so it still renders.
